official.deadline_note: The admission file for the Global Studies bachelor's programme in Studielink must be complete, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026; any programme handling fee is due by 10 December 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year; scholarship applications open 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027
official.status_note: Official page states: 'Applications are open from 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published as 'Tuition fees - At cost per academic year*', arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk.
benefits: Living expenses of EUR 20,150 per academic year (EUR 1,550 per month), paid to students by the UM International Services Desk, broken down as housing EUR 960, groceries and personal hygiene EUR 160, telephone EUR 60, travel EUR 100, books and study materials EUR 90, clothing/hobbies and going out EUR 125, miscellaneous EUR 55
Tuition fees for the Global Studies bachelor's programme at cost per academic year, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk
Health and liability insurance at cost, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk
Visa application costs at cost, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk

UM Pre-Academic Training costs at cost (a two-week mandatory component of the scholarship in the first week of August 2027), plus International Student Ambassador Programme (ISAP) costs for the first block only
A UM room allocated to the scholar until 16 July 2028
eligibility: You hold the nationality of a country eligible to receive Official Development Assistance from the OECD (Surinam excluded) and meet the requirements for obtaining an entry visa and residence permit for the Netherlands
You do not have a dual nationality from an EU/EEA country, Switzerland or Surinam

You have applied for admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme at UM for the 2027-2028 academic year and submitted your application file in full, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026
You do not have a diploma from a higher education institution; you are not eligible if you have completed a degree programme equivalent to a bachelor degree
You are not older than 35 years of age on 1 September 2027

You agree to become an active Global Studies and UM ambassador during and after your studies, by committing to share your experiences during at least one (information) session for students and/or other stakeholders
requirements: Apply for admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme via Studielink and obtain a UM student ID number, which you need to complete and submit the scholarship application form
By the scholarship deadline of 1 February 2027 you must have met all registration requirements, except legal residence, tuition payment and a hard copy of a diploma
Pay any programme handling fee yourself by 10 December 2026; the UM International Services Desk does not cover handling fees
Accept the UM room allocated to you until 16 July 2028; refusing the room means your scholarship will be cancelled
Take part in the two-week mandatory UM Pre-Academic Training in the first week of August 2027
Submit only one application, with documents in .doc, .docx or PDF format, because UM cannot add or replace documents after you submit the application
documents: Curriculum Vitae, up to date and no longer than two A4 pages, containing education and (job) experience, proven previous extracurricular engagement with your previous (academic) organisation or high school, active citizenship in your community, and any awards or prizes received
Letter of motivation, completed using the UM template
Proof of academic excellence: latest grade transcript showing at least 75% of the maximum grade, for example a 3 out of 4, equivalent to a 7.5 out of 10 at Maastricht University

Personal statement of financial needs, explaining why you would benefit from the scholarship and describing personal circumstances such as financial difficulty, sole parent or caretaking responsibilities, medical condition, disability or refugee status

Reference letter dated and written no earlier than 1 February 2025, by a (former) professor, teacher, principal, college counsellor, lecturer or employer, not a family member, and following the UM scholarship reference letter guidelines
Contact details of one referee: relationship to the applicant, work telephone number including the applicable country calling code, and a work or institutional email address
selection_criteria: Top-performing bachelor students from eligible countries with personal development potential (published target group)
Demonstrable financial need, evidenced through the personal statement of financial needs
Continuous good to excellent results during prior (high school) education, shown by the latest grade transcript at 75% or more of the maximum grade
Personal development potential that can be uniquely supported by the Global Studies study programme
Proven extracurricular engagement with a previous (academic) organisation or high school and active citizenship in the community, evidenced in the CV
coverage: Tuition fees for the Global Studies bachelor's programme, at cost per academic year
Living expenses of EUR 20,150 per academic year (EUR 1,550 per month)
Health and liability insurance, at cost
UM Pre-Academic Training costs at cost, plus International Student Ambassador Programme (ISAP) costs for the first block only
Air tickets are not included and must be paid by the candidate; the cleaning fee of approximately EUR 75 is not included and has to be paid to Maastricht Housing upfront
application_method: Apply for admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme at Maastricht University through Studielink and receive your UM student ID number
Complete the admission tasks in the MyApplication portal (including uploading documents and paying any handling fee) so that your application file is complete before 10 December 2026

Log in with your UM account to the UM scholarship application form and upload the CV, motivation letter, grade transcript, personal statement of financial needs and reference letter, then submit once before the deadline

The UM International Services Desk checks whether all applications are complete after 1 February 2027; the UM Scholarship Office forwards the application to the Global Studies admission office, which ranks it on the UM scholarship selection criteria and proposes a top-5 to the Global Studies Scholarship selection committee in March 2027

The selection committee invites the top-5 applicants for an online interview; non-selected candidates are placed on a reserve list, all candidates are informed of their status in April 2027, and status is selected, waitlisted or rejected by the beginning of June 2027
Sign and return the award letter to the UM International Services Desk to accept the scholarship
official.application_route: Admission via Studielink for the Global Studies bachelor's, then the UM scholarship application form (log in with your UM account) with all documents uploaded, submitted once before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET
official.study_mode: Full time; September start in Maastricht
official.citizenship_residency: Nationality of an OECD ODA-eligible country (Surinam excluded), no dual nationality of an EU/EEA country, Switzerland or Surinam, and able to meet the requirements for an entry visa and residence permit for the Netherlands
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is restricted to non-EU/EEA nationals of OECD ODA-eligible countries; the UM scholarship overview table lists the nationality requirement for this award as 'Non-EU/EEA'
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must be (conditionally) admitted to the Global Studies bachelor's programme at Maastricht University for 2027-2028
official.duration: 36 months for the bachelor's programme in Global Studies
official.description: The UM NL Global Studies Scholarship offers one full coverage scholarship, including a tuition fee waiver and monthly stipend, per academic year for top-performing bachelor students from eligible countries with personal development potential who have been (conditionally) admitted to the Global Studies programme. The Global Studies bachelor trains students to understand and develop solutions for complex global issues, crossing disciplinary and geographical boundaries, and is unique in the Netherlands in having six faculties contribute equally to its educational content.
official.english_requirement: Academic IELTS 6.0 overall; TOEFL iBT 80 (obtained before 2026) or 4.5 (obtained from 2026); Pearson PTE Academic minimum 61; LanguageCert Academic minimum 65; TOEIC listening and reading 865 with speaking and writing 335; Cambridge First B2 Grade B or C, or Cambridge C1 Advanced, or Cambridge C2 Proficiency. Certificates are accepted only if no more than two years old on the programme start date, and IELTS Academic Online or TOEFL iBT Home Edition are accepted only where an onsite test centre cannot be reached or is closed for safety reasons. You are exempt with a Dutch VWO diploma, a VWO-equivalent EU/EEA secondary diploma where you followed English through the final year, a secondary diploma from a country where English is an official language and the language of instruction, a bachelor's degree taught solely in English, or an International or European Baccalaureate, US high school diploma or UK GCE A-levels.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a single-place full ride for the three-year Global Studies bachelor's at Maastricht: UM pays your tuition at cost, arranges and pays health and liability insurance, visa application costs and the two-week pre-academic training, and transfers EUR 20,150 a year (EUR 1,550 a month) for living costs, plus a UM room until 16 July 2028. The real bottleneck is sequencing, not the scholarship form itself: you must first build a complete admission file for Global Studies in Studielink before 10 December 2026, and the scholarship form only unlocks once UM issues your student ID. Only one scholarship submission is accepted and documents cannot be swapped afterwards, so every file should be final before you click submit. Treat the 1 February 2027 deadline as the last step of a process you really start in October 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recent secondary-school graduate from an OECD ODA-eligible country with strong grades, demonstrable financial need and a record of community engagement who wants an interdisciplinary, English-taught social-science bachelor's.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the Global Studies application in Studielink early enough that your UM student number arrives well before December, because the scholarship form cannot be started without it
Prepare a latest grade transcript that clearly shows at least 75% of the maximum grade, and have it translated or certified if it is not already in English or Dutch

Send your referee the UM reference letter guidelines and request a letter dated on or after 1 February 2025 from a professor, teacher, principal, college counsellor, lecturer or employer, never a relative
Draft the motivation letter on UM's own template and the financial-needs statement separately, since they answer different questions and both are mandatory
Budget for the handling fee charged on non-EU/EEA curriculum diplomas and pay it by 10 December 2026, because UM does not reimburse it
Check that your passport, or your Schengen residence permit, stays valid beyond 2 September 2027, otherwise you must apply from your home country through an MVV visa route
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 10 December 2026 admission-file deadline: without a complete admission file the scholarship is out of reach even if you file the scholarship form on time
A reference letter that ignores the UM guidelines, is dated before 1 February 2025, or lists only a personal email address for the referee, which makes the application incomplete
A CV longer than two A4 pages, or one that omits extracurricular engagement and active citizenship, the exact evidence the target group asks for
Assuming the single-submission rule leaves room to correct a document later, which it does not
Holding a bachelor-equivalent degree already, or holding EU/EEA, Swiss or Surinamese nationality including dual nationality, which are absolute exclusions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to the Netherlands and the roughly EUR 75 cleaning fee payable upfront to Maastricht Housing are not covered, the programme handling fee is not reimbursed, and travel to collect an MVV visa is on you. From 17 July 2028 you must fund your own housing for the remaining years, even though the EUR 960 a month housing line in the stipend is calculated around the allocated UM room; UM also states the EUR 20,150 living figure is subject to change for 2028-2029.
document_audit: The motivation letter must be built on UM's template, so a free-form letter risks being treated as non-compliant
Referee details must state the relationship, a work telephone number with country calling code and a work or institutional email address; a personal email is rejected unless a valid reason is given
You upload the reference letter yourself, because UM does not accept documents sent directly by the referee
Files must be .doc, .docx or PDF, and since only one submission is possible everything should be converted and checked before uploading

Separately, programme admission requires a portrait photo meeting UM specifications, a passport copy, transcript and diploma copies, and a permission-for-document-verification form if your diploma is not verified by DUO
alerts: The scholarship portal is unavailable between 22 and 26 October 2026 for an upgrade, so do not plan a last-minute submission
Refusing the allocated UM room cancels the scholarship outright, and the room is not suitable for partners, spouses, children or pets
By 1 February 2027 you must have met all registration requirements except legal residence, tuition payment and the hard copy of your diploma
Results arrive in stages: completeness check after 1 February, top-5 interviews in March, status notified in April, and waitlists resolved by June 2027, so earlier silence is not a rejection
You must agree to act as a Global Studies and UM ambassador, including at least one information session, during and after your studies
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for Global Studies in Studielink, complete the MyApplication admission tasks and handling fee, log in with your UM account to the UM scholarship application form, upload all documents once, and submit before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET.
